name: RBI and SEBI Expectations for AI
question: What will my financial regulator ask about our AI?
summary: RBI’s FREE-AI framework (August 2025) sets seven sutras and recommendations for banks and NBFCs: a board-approved AI policy, an AI inventory, audits, customer disclosure and grievance routes, and incident reporting. RBI’s draft model risk guidance (June 2026) extends model governance to AI, including third-party models, kill switches and human oversight. SEBI’s Regulation 16C (February 2025) makes intermediaries solely responsible for AI output, data and compliance, and SEBI has announced guidelines with kill switches and human-in-the-loop controls.
useCases: Banks, NBFCs, brokers and other regulated entities using AI
When a vendor supplies the model

steps.text: Name, owner, purpose, model and vendor. Sahyog Securities expected 6 uses and found 23.

steps.title: Tier by customer impact
steps.text: Internal tools, customer-facing agents and agents that decide about customers need different controls. The gaps function shows what each system still lacks.

steps.title: A vendor model is still yours
steps.text: SEBI’s Regulation 16C makes the intermediary solely responsible for AI output and data; RBI’s draft model guidance expects vendor models to be validated too.

steps.title: A kill switch without a deploy
steps.text: A feature flag per system lets operations stop it in seconds and hand requests to people. Both regulators have signalled kill switches.

steps.title: Humans decide the high-impact cases
steps.text: For decision-tier systems such as KYC rejection or credit, the agent recommends and a person decides.

steps.title: Tell the customer
steps.text: Customer-facing answers say AI is involved and offer a route to a human and to grievance redress, as FREE-AI recommends.

practice.scenario: Sahyog Securities, a fictional broker with an NBFC arm, prepared for a regulator’s review of its AI use. Its first inventory found 23 AI uses, not the 6 the team expected. Four were customer-facing, and two ran on a vendor model with no audit rights in the contract. It adopted a board-approved AI policy, tiered every use by customer impact, validated the vendor models itself, and put kill switches and customer disclosure on the four customer-facing agents.

library.name: OpenFeature
library.what: A vendor-neutral feature-flag standard; a flag per AI system gives operations a kill switch that works without a deploy.

practice.note: Regulation 16C makes the intermediary solely responsible for AI output even when a vendor supplies the model. Track the final SEBI guidelines and RBI model risk directions, which were not final on 26 Sep 2026.

numericDrill.question: A broker has 20 internal AI tools, 3 customer-facing agents and 2 agents that make decisions about customers. If the controls required per system are 3 for internal, 7 for customer-facing and 8 for decision tiers, how many control instances must it evidence?
numericDrill.answer: 20 × 3 + 3 × 7 + 2 × 8 = 60 + 21 + 16 = 97. Tiering matters: treating all 25 as decision-tier would mean 200, and treating all as internal would leave the customer-facing agents short of kill switches, disclosure and review.

interview.question: What does SEBI Regulation 16C mean for a broker using a vendor’s LLM?
interview.answer: It makes the regulated entity solely responsible for the privacy and security of investor data, for the output of the AI tools it relies on, and for compliance with law, whether the tool is built in-house or bought. Vendor assurances do not transfer that responsibility, so the broker must validate the model, control the data it receives and keep audit rights in the contract.

interview.question: What does RBI’s FREE-AI framework ask of a bank deploying an agent?
interview.answer: It sets seven principles, or sutras, and recommendations under six pillars. For a deployment that means a board-approved AI policy, an inventory of AI uses by risk, independent testing and audit, telling customers when AI is involved and giving them a way to contest outcomes, incident reporting, and accountability that does not shrink as the system becomes more autonomous.
